note: Rules, preferences and guardrails with explicit lifecycles. A rule that belongs to a program retires when that program completes - the model must never tell Lane in 2028 that he is violating a California Launch Fund rule.

authority_hierarchy.label: Lane's explicit current instruction
authority_hierarchy.note: Beats everything below it, including this model's own reasoning.

authority_hierarchy.label: Verified external fact
authority_hierarchy.note: A document from outside this model: statement, offer, lease, written quote, official policy.

authority_hierarchy.label: Historical pattern
authority_hierarchy.note: Useful for planning. Never an SLA, never a promise.

authority_hierarchy.label: Agent inference
authority_hierarchy.note: Lowest authority by design. An inference may surface a conflict; it may never silently overrule a decision.

authority_rule: When two sources disagree, the lower level number wins and the conflict is reported, never silently resolved. An inference that contradicts a decision becomes a review trigger, not an override.

lifecycles.enduring_preference: How Lane wants to live. Outlives every program. Retires only when Lane says so.
lifecycles.active_guardrail: A live constraint with a scope. Retires when its scope ends or Lane lifts it.
lifecycles.temporary_rule: Deliberately short-lived - an experiment or a push. Carries a review date.
lifecycles.project_decision: A choice that belongs to one program and retires with it.
lifecycles.current_assumption: A modeled value, not a rule. Listed here only when it is being treated as one.
lifecycles.external_fact: Something the world decided. Retires when the date passes or the fact changes.
lifecycles.future_review: A scheduled reconsideration. Fires once, then becomes a decision.

rules.statement: Preserve financial optionality. Do not trade durable flexibility for a short-term convenience.
Money needed inside a short horizon must be cash-like, not volatile single-stock exposure.
Klein and Tilly travel in the climate-controlled cabin, restrained, never in a truck bed. Optimize travel for their safety, not for speed.
rules.override_rule: Hard constraint. Only Lane may relax it, explicitly.

rules.statement: Unknown values stay TBD or ranged. Never manufacture precision, never promote a research lead to a verified fact.
Never report a liquidity requirement as a cost. Spend, refundable cash, reserve capital, contingency and recurring exposure are always reported separately.
The model may calculate and recommend irreversible actions. It may never treat one as decided without Lane's explicit approval.
The emergency fund is not program capital and is never counted toward the California Launch Fund.
Maximum acceptable modeled average Orlando rental subsidy is $350/month.
Employer relocation coverage is modeled at zero until stated in writing - and self-funding is never assumed either.
rules.expires_when: relocation support is stated in writing

rules.statement: March 2027 is a North Star, not permission to make a bad decision. No irreversible commitment before Gate 1 and Gate 2.
Do not evaluate whether California was a mistake during the first 14 days after arrival.
Do not invent or infer a one-time brokerage transfer amount that Lane has never confirmed.
rules.note: Recorded as a rule rather than a task. It is a standing constraint; it is never 'done'.

rules.statement: Recruiting threads are never merged without a requisition ID proving they are one.
Hold $350/week for all food including Factor.
rules.review_trigger: Review after the Venture X balance is cleared, or if the experiment stops holding
rules.note: An experiment, not a permanent standard of living.

rules.statement: $300 per Disney paycheck to Venture X, stretching to $400-500 only when fixed bills and the cash floor are protected.
rules.successor_rule: Redirect the payoff habit into the Launch Fund once the card is materially reduced.

rules.statement: Hiring-manager interview with Cherie Hurwitz, 2026-09-15, 5:00-5:45 PM ET.
Reconsider keeping or selling the Tundra once California parking, fuel, commute and utilization are known.
Revisit renting versus buying in California after the first lease term.
